headline: Figma's AI Agents Go Live
subheadline: Figma just dropped a live event on co-designing with AI agents, Cursor shipped an SDK for teams, and there's a killer conference recording library on agentic design systems — all directly relevant to what you're building.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma's May Release: Co-designing with AI Agents, Voice-to-Text in Make, and Zapier Connector
sections.description: Big one. Figma's May release notes include live demos of teams co-designing with AI agents, plus Make gets voice-to-text prompts, question cards, version history, and a Zapier connector for pulling in external app data. The agent workflow demos could directly inform how you architect your white-label sport apps system — especially if agents can eventually manipulate components and tokens.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma AI in 2026: Everything It Can Do — and What It Still Can't
sections.description: A clear-eyed rundown of where Figma AI actually stands right now — content generation, image editing, UI drafting, code handoff, full-site creation. Useful as a reality check for what you can lean on vs. where your MCP + Claude integration fills gaps Figma's native AI doesn't cover yet.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Cursor SDK — Build Custom AI Agents for Your Team's Codebase
sections.description: Cursor just launched their SDK in public beta, letting teams build and deploy custom AI agents for PR security reviews, vulnerability scanning, and more — with MCP support baked in. Given you're already in Cursor daily, this could be interesting for automating repetitive code checks on your vibe-coded projects, or even connecting Cursor agents to your Figma MCP pipeline.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: AI Design Systems Conference 2026 — 15+ Hours of Recordings Now Available
sections.description: The sold-out AI Design Systems Conference (speakers from Figma, Adobe, WhatsApp, Miro) has released all recordings. Covers agentic design systems, MCP integrations, vibe coding, and shipping production-ready work. This is essentially a masterclass library for exactly the intersection you're working at. Cherry-pick the MCP and agentic design system talks first.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: The Future of Enterprise Design Systems: 2026 Trends for Agentic AI
sections.description: Supernova makes the case that design systems in 2026 are evolving from static libraries into agentic platforms — systems that can automate, self-maintain, and scale. Includes a practical roadmap. Directly relevant to your white-label system architecture: think about what happens when AI agents can consume your tokens and components autonomously.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Agentic UX — When Products Become Execution Layers
sections.description: Two pieces converge on this: products are shifting from tools users operate to execution layers where AI agents act on users' behalf. The designer's new job isn't just crafting interfaces — it's designing the trust model, guardrails, and override patterns for autonomous agents. As someone thinking about product leadership, this is the design philosophy shift that will define the next era.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: OpenAI Codex + Figma: The Code-to-Design Loop via MCP
sections.description: OpenAI's Codex now connects to Figma through the MCP server, enabling a running-UI-to-Figma-frames workflow. You're already building your own Claude + Figma MCP integration — worth understanding the Codex approach to see if there are architectural patterns (or pitfalls) you can learn from. The MCP ecosystem is getting crowded fast.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If AI agents can manipulate your design system autonomously, what's the designer's role?
sections.description: With Figma launching agent co-design workflows, Cursor shipping agent SDKs, and design systems going agentic — the question isn't whether agents will touch your design system, it's when. Your MCP project puts you ahead of most designers here. The career question: does this make you more of a systems architect than a visual designer? And is that the product leadership path you want?
